concepts.label: cbepctl
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - referenced here for the cross-tool comparison below; the concept is minted (and given fuller treatment) in this same batch's cbepctl-intro.json, not yet promoted

relations.subject: tool:cbstats
relations.evidence: The `host` must be the hostname or IP address of a node within the cluster. The port must be `11210`.

relations.subject: service:data-service
relations.evidence: The `cbstats` tool provides Data Service statistics, for an individual, specified node.

notable_absence.finding: The common-options table documents -u/-p/-S (username, password, read-password-from-stdin) but never states which Couchbase RBAC role or privilege those credentials must carry to retrieve Data Service stats - despite this tool exposing per-bucket, per-vBucket internals the Web Console does not surface (per the tool's own registry description). This is the third page in this batch (with cbcollect-info-tool.md and cbepctl-intro.md) to accept authentication credentials without ever naming a required role, a consistent pattern across this round's diagnostic-tool pages.

cross_component_finding: cbstats and cbepctl (this batch's other per-node/per-bucket control tool - see cbepctl-intro.json) both connect over the identical port:11210 and share nearly the same common-option flag set (-a, -b, -u, -p, -S), despite documenting entirely separate operations (read-only stats retrieval vs. persistence/vBucket-state control). Neither page cross-references the other or acknowledges the shared connection mechanism, suggesting both are thin CLI wrappers over the same underlying memcached-binary-protocol client library - a fact neither page states.
cross_product_finding: The page is unambiguously Server-only (a raw KV-port tool with no REST/UI equivalent mentioned); Capella does not expose port 11210 to customers for this kind of direct per-node stats access, though the page gives no such caveat since it has no Capella-facing counterpart to distinguish itself from.
